title: Do you think I’m right?  Or is this still a plot hole? #Wicked #Wicke...
transcript: How can Nessa read the grimmary in wicked for good? I have seen a lot of people asking this question and pointing to it as a potential plot hole, but I honestly think there is a somewhat straightforward explanation, because this scene comes directly after the scene where Alphabet enchants Nessa Rose's slippers. While we do not know the specifics of what this spell does, one potential interpretation is that it grants your heart's desires. Whatever you are wanting in the moment, it can make that happen. So when Nessa is wanting to go back to the time at the Ozda's ballroom when she felt like she was floating on air, it can make her fly. But then when she is getting angry at Bok, suddenly the thing that she wants is to be able to cast a spell to take his heart away. what I think happened is that she is able to tap into Alice's magic that has been imbued into her slippers to cast the spell. Obviously a very rudimentary version. We see Alice saying, you're not doing it right, but there is enough magic in the slippers to be able to cast a very haphazard version of the spell. I don't really know if this logic necessarily works for the musical, as in the musical, the spell that Alphabet cast on the slippers is specifically to make her walk. But when it comes to the movies, I think that you could say that it is A direct result of the spell that Alphabet cast on the slippers
